title: The Bird-Singing Contests That Are Fueling a Conservation Crisis
author: Sandy Ong
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyThe Bird-Singing Contests That Are Fueling a Conservation CrisisMillions of Southeast Asian songbirds are trapped and trafficked every yearSOBy Sandy Ong5:00 PM CDT on July 20, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThis article originally appeared in Knowable Magazine.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 00:00/01:0610205.7K 350The World Is Facing a Huge Plastic Crisis in the OceansShareNextStayOn a Sunday afternoon in April, the main minibus terminal in Sukabumi, Indonesia, looked sleepy from the outside. But in an open space round the back, hundreds of men were gathered. Amid chatter and cigarette smoke, the air buzzed with excitement, for one of the region’s biggest bird-singing competitions was set to begin, and a motorbike was among the prizes.As the day progressed, dozens of songbirds were brought out for their 10-minute rounds, from tiny garden sunbirds and grey-cheeked bulbuls to larger oriental magpie-robins and orange-headed thrushes.
